ai.definition: Nuclear fusion is a process where atomic nuclei combine to form heavier nuclei, releasing vast amounts of energy in the process. Recent advancements focus on achieving this process under controlled conditions to generate electricity.
ai.howItWorks: Fusion technologies use either magnetic confinement or laser-driven compression to heat and compress hydrogen isotopes (like deuterium and tritium) until they reach temperatures where fusion occurs, releasing energy.
ai.problemSolved: Current energy sources like fossil fuels contribute significantly to climate change. Fusion offers a potential solution by providing clean, nearly limitless energy without carbon emissions.
ai.manufacturing: Manufacturing fusion reactors involves complex engineering challenges such as materials selection and plasma confinement system design.
ai.buildProcess: The build process includes designing the reactor, constructing the physical structure, installing and testing components like magnets or lasers, and finally conducting experiments to achieve sustained fusion reactions.
ai.costDrivers: High initial R&D costs, expensive materials, and complex engineering are significant cost drivers. Long-term costs could be reduced with successful commercialization.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The outlook is promising but uncertain due to the technical challenges that need to be overcome before widespread adoption.
ai.regulation: Current regulatory frameworks may not fully address the unique safety and environmental considerations of fusion reactors. New regulations might be required as this technology advances.
ai.risks: Technical risks include achieving sustained fusion reactions, managing radioactive waste, and ensuring reactor safety. Economic risks involve high initial costs and potential long-term financial viability concerns.
ai.profitability: Profitability is uncertain but could be significant if the technology becomes commercially viable. Revenue streams might come from electricity sales or licensing of technologies.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future development will likely focus on improving efficiency, reducing costs, and addressing safety and environmental concerns to make fusion a practical energy source.

glossary.def: A method of containing plasma using strong magnetic fields, typically used in tokamaks and stellarators.
Using high-intensity lasers to compress fuel pellets containing hydrogen isotopes to achieve fusion conditions.
A state of matter where atoms are ionized, consisting of free electrons and ions.
A toroidal device used for magnetic confinement of plasma in nuclear fusion research.

subsystems.name: Confinement system
subsystems.role: holds the fuel together long enough and densely enough for nuclei to fuse.
parts: magnetic coils (tokamak, stellarator) or laser and pulsed-power drivers (inertial)

subsystems.name: Heating and fuelling
subsystems.role: drives the fuel to fusion temperature — over 100 million °C for magnetic schemes.

subsystems.name: First wall and blanket
subsystems.role: absorbs the neutron energy, shields the structure and breeds fresh tritium from lithium.

subsystems.name: Exhaust
subsystems.role: strips heat and helium 'ash' from the reacting region before it damages anything.
parts: divertor targets, or the target chamber wall and tritium recovery in inertial designs

subsystems.name: Tritium plant
subsystems.role: separates, stores and re-injects tritium, because it decays and is extremely scarce.

subsystems.name: Control and diagnostics
subsystems.role: senses the reaction thousands of times a second and steers it away from instabilities.

buildSteps.title: Pick the confinement route
buildSteps.detail: Magnetic (a bottle of field lines) and inertial (compress a tiny fuel capsule with lasers or pulsed power) need completely different machines.

buildSteps.title: Build the containment
buildSteps.detail: Wind and assemble the superconducting coils, or build the laser hall, optics and target chamber.

buildSteps.title: Install the chamber wall
buildSteps.detail: Fit the first wall and divertor or target surfaces from materials that survive intense neutron and heat loads.

buildSteps.title: Add heating and fuelling
buildSteps.detail: Beam lines, antennas and pellet injectors are aligned to the reaction region.

buildSteps.title: Close the fuel loop
buildSteps.detail: Wrap the chamber in a lithium blanket and connect it to a tritium extraction plant so the plant makes its own fuel.

buildSteps.title: Connect heat to a turbine
buildSteps.detail: Coolant carries blanket heat to heat exchangers and a generator — the step that turns a physics experiment into a power station.

buildSteps.title: Commission with hydrogen
buildSteps.detail: Start on ordinary hydrogen or deuterium, then deuterium–tritium, learning to control the reaction without damaging the machine.

buildSteps.title: Prove net electricity and reliability
buildSteps.detail: Run for long periods and show that output exceeds everything the plant consumes.

prerequisites.tech: Net energy gain from a fusion reaction
prerequisites.why: a laser facility first released more fusion energy than the laser delivered in 2022, but magnetic devices have not yet done so.
stronger fields shrink and cheapen a tokamak; high-temperature superconductors have only recently reached the needed field strengths.
no tested material yet survives years of neutron bombardment inside a power plant.

prerequisites.tech: Tritium breeding and handling at scale
prerequisites.why: tritium is scarce and radioactive with a short half-life, so a plant must breed and recycle its own.
inertial schemes need lasers or pulsed power that fire many times a second at high efficiency, not a few shots a day.

pathway.milestone: laser-driven ignition demonstrated; large magnetic test reactor under assembly in France
pathway.unlocks: confidence that the physics can work at reactor scale.

pathway.milestone: burning plasmas sustained for long periods, with tritium breeding blanket modules tested
pathway.unlocks: data on materials, fuel self-sufficiency and heat removal.

pathway.milestone: pilot plants that deliver electricity to a grid
pathway.unlocks: engineering proof that a fusion station can run and be maintained.

pathway.milestone: commercial fleets, if materials, tritium and reliability are all solved
pathway.unlocks: firm, low-carbon baseload power with no long-lived waste.
